issue.title: Encoding of `duration` unit suffixes is incorrect for wide streams

discussion.p: specifies operator<< for `duration` as if by:

For `Period::type` equal to `micro`, units-suffix is implementation-defined to be either `"μs"` (`"\u00b5\u0073"`) or `"us"`.
The type and encoding of units-suffix are not specified in terms of `charT`. In particular, if `"μs"` denotes an ordinary string literal, then for a wide stream the expression above inserts a `const char*` into a basic_ostream<wchar_t>. specifies this operation by applying `out.widen()` to each individual `char`.
This does not perform transcoding. For example, when the ordinary literal encoding is UTF-8, the micro sign is represented by multiple char code units. Widening those code units individually does not produce the corresponding micro sign in the wide literal encoding.
For example:

when the implementation chooses the `μs` representation, but the current specification does not provide semantics that produce that result.
The same problem affects `%q` in , whose replacement is specified as "the duration's unit suffix as specified in ".
This is similar to LWG , which clarified that formatting to `wchar_t` requires transcoding rather than widening narrow code units.
The unit suffix should therefore be specified directly as a sequence of `charT`, using the literal encoding associated with `charT`.
